raw_response:
I’m on 6 mu total, so I can’t take big risks. Same wheat-maize rotation as usual. I’ve farmed this land a long time, and with only one person in the house, I need things I can manage myself and on time. Wheat and maize both still make sense here because the system is familiar, the land suits it, and if I keep the timing tight after wheat harvest, I can still get a decent maize crop. I’ve got well water, so I’m not fully at the mercy of the rain, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too casually. For wheat, I’ll use a common improved variety from the local dealer, sow in early October, put most fertilizer down at planting, then add some urea around jointing if the stand looks a little weak or yellow. For maize, I’ll plant right after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed, give it a base fertilizer plus one topdress around the big growth stage, and water if the weather turns dry. I do a bit more than the minimum on fertilizer because if I save too much there and yield falls, that hurts more than spending a little extra. But I still keep it within what a small farmer like me can afford.
